results.fact: Which way to go at the Rampart Ridge junction (Rampart Lakes boulder gully vs the Lila Lake side)
results.evidence: The approach says to go right at the ridge junction for Lila Lake/Alta, then in the same sentence sends the party south through the Rampart Lakes basin to a boulder gully and a 5,570 ft saddle before turning west; the beta instead says the climbers' path leaves at a cairn near the Rachel/Lila junction. The trail-association page says to go RIGHT toward Lila Lake at the ridge, 0.3 mi to a cairned junction, and take the climbers' path left up the south ridge; Alta's summit lies north of the junction while the Rampart Lakes lie south. Only one external source describes the junction in detail, and fixing it means rewriting the approach, the approach variant, the saddle waypoint and the climbing route, so it is flagged, not patched. Separately (not a field contradiction): the 18 Sep 2026 Three Queens Fire order lists Rachel Lake Trailhead and Rachel Lake Trail 1313 as closed through 31 Oct 2026, while access.closures is null.

results.evidence: The reader assumed FR 6835 was the outlier, but the peak's climbing page says to drive 4.7 mi up the Foss road, turn left onto FR 6835, and park about 0.5 mi on, 200 ft past a small concrete bridge, across from the toe of the north ridge. OpenStreetMap road data shows FR 68 (Foss River Road, FS 6800) ends at a gate by the main Foss bridge, and the bridge over the East Fork Foss River (15 m from the river line) is on FS 6835, West Fork Foss Road. The Forest Service and trail-association pages for West Fork Foss both put the FR 6835 turn at 4.7 mi on FR 68, and a trip report parks just after the East Fork bridge at mile 5.2 (4.7 + 0.5). Note: the trailhead waypoint pin itself (47.6114,-121.2426) lies on the Necklace Valley Trail about 4.5 km south of that bridge; pin positions are out of scope and it is not moved.

results.evidence: The Forest Service page for Dutch Miller Gap Trail 1030 starts at the Dingford Creek Trailhead gate (12 + ~5 mi up FS 56, the same drive the row describes) with mileposts at 7.7 (horse camp), 14.2 (Williams Lake junction) and about 15.2 at the gap. An independent trail atlas says a gate installed at Dingford Creek in 2007 added 7.5 mi of road walking to reach the gap. The 2003 ascent report that supplies the 22 mi round trip and the 4.8 h to the gap started from the old road end. So the 15 mi one-way is current and the 22 mi, the 11 mi summit waypoint and the 4.8 h approach time are stale; the approach time is nulled rather than recomputed. Not patched: gain_ft 5400 is also from the 2003 start and likely understates the gain from Dingford.
